author: priya
body: We wrap errors with the operation name before returning them — fmt.Errorf("load order %d: %w", id, err). A bare return err gives on-call a stack with no idea which call failed. This has bitten us twice in the payments path.

author: marcus
body: Same note as last week: please wrap this error with context. `return err` here means the alert just says 'connection refused' with nothing about which downstream.

author: priya
body: Every handler needs an explicit timeout on outbound calls. We had an incident in March where one slow partner API held the entire worker pool. Default is no timeout, which means infinite.

author: dana
body: Add a timeout here. Team rule since the March incident — no unbounded outbound calls, ever.

author: marcus
body: Module-level mutable state again. We keep these on an injected object so tests do not leak into each other. We spent a whole sprint untangling the last set of globals.

author: priya
body: This global cache will make the tests order-dependent. Pass it in through the constructor like the other stores do.

author: dana
body: No f-strings in SQL, even when the value looks internal. Parameterise everything — we do not make case-by-case judgements about whether a value is trusted.

author: priya
body: Parameterise this query. The rule is absolute here, no exceptions for admin-only paths.

author: marcus
body: New public functions on the auth package need a doc comment saying what happens on failure. Callers keep assuming these raise when they actually return None.

author: dana
body: What does this return when the token is expired? Please document the failure mode — this is the third time someone has had to read the body to find out.

author: priya
body: Do not catch bare Exception and continue. If you genuinely want to skip a bad record, catch the specific error and log the record id, otherwise we lose real failures silently.

author: marcus
body: Bare except with pass. Same objection as PR 891 — this hides real failures. Catch what you expect and log the rest.
